neighborhoods.name: Yanaka
neighborhoods.character: Old Tokyo that survived the earthquakes and bombs. Low wooden houses, independent shops, a cemetery with 7,000 graves, cats everywhere, artisans, a 350-year-old shotengai (shopping street). Locals are genuinely happy to see visitors who venture this far.

neighborhoods.name: Shimokitazawa
neighborhoods.character: Tokyo's neighborhood for secondhand vinyl, vintage clothing, tiny theaters, and live music. Young Tokyoites come here to be themselves. No chain stores permitted by neighborhood agreement. Jazz from open doorways.

neighborhoods.name: Shibuya/Shinjuku
neighborhoods.character: The Tokyo of every photograph — neon, crowds, the crossing, department stores going 15 floors. Overwhelming but essential. Best experienced at night when the scale becomes comprehensible and beautiful.

neighborhoods.name: Yanesen (Yanaka-Nezu-Sendagi)
neighborhoods.character: Three interconnected old-Tokyo neighborhoods forming the most atmospheric area in the city. Nezu Shrine predates Edo. Independent shops selling handmade things. The 'shotengai' (market street) has been in constant operation since 1900.

neighborhoods.name: Koenji
neighborhoods.character: Tokyo's coolest neighborhood that most tourists never find. Subcultures — punk, anime, alternative, vintage. More secondhand shops per square meter than anywhere in Tokyo. The covered shopping street (shotengai) is lined with tiny restaurants serving everything.

experiences.name: Tsukiji outer market breakfast
experiences.description: The inner tuna auction moved to Toyosu, but the outer market remains unchanged since 1935. At 7am: sushi that was alive 2 hours ago, tamagoyaki (sweet omelet) hot off the grill, dashi broth in a paper cup. This is the best breakfast in Tokyo.
experiences.why_this_matters: No restaurant can replicate the freshness of eating sushi 50 meters from where it was unloaded. This is a sensory education in Japanese food culture.
experiences.practical_tips: Arrive by 7:30am before the best stalls sell out. Bring cash. The outer market is free to enter. Don't eat sushi from the touristy places with photos — look for the ones with no English.

experiences.name: Yanaka neighborhood wandering
experiences.description: Yanaka Ginza shotengai (the old shopping street) at 10am: the pickled vegetable seller opens her sliding door, the sembei maker fans charcoal, a cat sits on a roof. This is old Shitamachi (low city) Tokyo — the Tokyo of a century ago, inexplicably surviving.
experiences.why_this_matters: Most of Tokyo was destroyed in 1923 (earthquake) or 1945 (bombing) and rebuilt modern. Yanaka survived both. Walking here is as close as you'll get to pre-war Tokyo. It's the most emotionally resonant neighborhood in the city.
experiences.practical_tips: Start at Nippori station. Walk down Yanaka Ginza, then into the cemetery, then south to Nezu Shrine. Allow 2-3 hours of real wandering. The tiny galleries and workshops are worth every open door you can find.

experiences.name: Shibuya Crossing at night
experiences.description: 2,000 people crossing simultaneously from all directions when the light changes — and no one collides. From above (Shibuya Sky or the free Mag's Park) the scale becomes visible. The neon, the chaos, the order beneath the chaos. This is Tokyo's self-portrait.
experiences.why_this_matters: Shibuya Crossing at night is one of the genuinely moving spectacles in modern cities. It represents something profound about Japanese society — 2,000 strangers, perfect chaos, perfect order. See it once.
experiences.practical_tips: Go at 8-9pm on a Friday for peak crowd. For the overhead view, Mag's Park on Shibuya Mark City gives a free view. Shibuya Sky observation deck requires a ticket but is higher.

experiences.name: Nezu Shrine torii gates in morning mist
experiences.description: One of Tokyo's oldest shrines (founded 1706), with a tunnel of vermillion torii gates winding up the hillside. At 7am, before the tourist buses arrive from Fushimi Inari in Kyoto, it belongs to you and the local dog walkers.
experiences.why_this_matters: While tourists queue for hours at Fushimi Inari in Kyoto, Nezu has the same experience, in Tokyo, with almost no one there. The 2-minute torii tunnel at dawn is one of Tokyo's most transcendent experiences.
experiences.practical_tips: Go before 9am. The gate tunnel is a 5-minute walk from the main shrine. Free entry. The azalea festival in April-May transforms the hillside into something extraordinary.

experiences.name: Depachika (department store basement food hall)
experiences.description: Japanese department store basements are the greatest food halls in the world — literally underground floors of lacquered bento boxes, wagashi (Japanese sweets), miso varieties, fresh tofu, sake from every prefecture. Go to Isetan in Shinjuku or Mitsukoshi in Ginza.
experiences.why_this_matters: The depachika is a Japanese cultural institution that has no equivalent anywhere else. The level of craft and presentation applied to food packaging is itself an art form.
experiences.practical_tips: Go around 4pm when 'time discount' stickers start appearing on bento boxes. Everything is presented as if it costs 10x what it does. The basement of Isetan Shinjuku is considered the best in Tokyo.

experiences.name: Shimokitazawa vintage record and clothes shopping
experiences.description: Shimokitazawa is the antithesis of Harajuku. Secondhand vinyl that costs ¥200. Vintage Levi's from the 1970s. A jazz record shop run by a man who has never sold anything he doesn't personally believe in. No chain stores. No tourist buses.
experiences.why_this_matters: This is Tokyo's creative underground — the counter-culture that exists beneath the surface of Shibuya's neon. It's a neighborhood with genuine personality.
experiences.practical_tips: Shimokitazawa station (Keio Inokashira or Odakyu line). Walk in any direction. The area around the old station building (re:built since 2019) has the best concentration of shops.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple at 6am
experiences.description: Tokyo's most famous temple is a tourist stampede during the day. At 6am: priests doing morning rituals, incense smoke rising into silence, older Tokyoites praying before work. The Nakamise shopping street is completely empty. The temple belongs to the devout.
experiences.why_this_matters: Senso-ji at dawn shows you what Tokyo was before modern Japan — an ancient city of ritual, incense, and prayer. The contrast with daytime crowds is complete.
experiences.practical_tips: 6am is the right time. The temple opens 24 hours. Clap twice, bow, make your prayer at the main hall. The omikuji (fortune slips) are worth trying — bad fortune means you tie it to the rack.

experiences.name: Ramen at a standing counter at midnight
experiences.description: A Shinjuku backstreet ramen shop at midnight, eating tonkotsu broth while salarymen loosen their ties beside you. Japanese ramen culture is one of the most sophisticated food cultures in the world. A bowl of ramen that has been in development for 20 years, at a counter where you eat alone and in silence.
experiences.why_this_matters: Ramen is not fast food in Japan — it's the result of a chef's lifetime of refinement. Understanding this transforms the act of eating it.
experiences.practical_tips: Shinjuku is the best ramen district in Tokyo. Look for shops with long lines even at midnight — that's the signal. Buy your ticket from the vending machine before entering. Some shops have English menus.

experiences.name: Hamarikyu Gardens tea ceremony
experiences.description: A 17th-century feudal lord's garden in the shadow of Tokyo's skyscrapers — tidal ponds, seasonal flowers, pine trees shaped over 300 years. The waterside tea house serves matcha and wagashi (sweets) with a view of the pond.
experiences.why_this_matters: The contrast of ancient garden and modern skyline, best from the teahouse dock, is Tokyo's essential visual metaphor — the old city and the new in the same frame.
experiences.practical_tips: Open 9am-5pm. ¥300 entry + ¥800 for tea. The garden connects to the Tokyo Bay ferry (to Asakusa) — a nice way to arrive or depart. Best in spring (cherry blossoms) or autumn.

experiences.name: Koenji shotengai and underground music
experiences.description: Koenji is where Tokyo's outsiders live — the punk scene, the vintage obsessives, the jazz musicians who play for audiences of 8 people. The shotengai (covered shopping street) leads to a maze of tiny bars, record shops, and restaurants where a meal costs ¥600.
experiences.why_this_matters: Every city has its underground. Tokyo's is in Koenji. If you're the kind of traveler who wants to understand a city's subculture rather than its surface, this is the neighborhood.
experiences.practical_tips: JR Chuo Line to Koenji station. The covered arcade north and south of the station is the starting point. Go in the afternoon — most venues open at 6pm. Ask in any record shop for live music that night.

experiences.name: Mount Takao sunrise hike
experiences.description: An hour from Shinjuku, Mount Takao (599m) is the most climbed mountain in the world — mostly by Tokyo locals. The summit offers a view of Mount Fuji on clear days. The trail passes an active Buddhist temple, a monkey park, and ancient cedar forest.
experiences.why_this_matters: Tokyo locals hike Takao the way New Yorkers go to Central Park. Being on the mountain at sunrise, when the city is still invisible below the mist, shows Tokyo's relationship with nature that the neon district hides.
experiences.practical_tips: Keio Takao Line from Shinjuku (50 min). Trail 1 is the most accessible. Take the cable car down if tired. Check the weather forecast — the Fuji view requires clear conditions. Pack lunch.

experiences.name: Yoyogi Park Sunday afternoon
experiences.description: Sunday afternoon Yoyogi Park is one of Tokyo's best free shows: amateur rockabilly dancers in 1950s costumes, families with picnic sheets, dogs in strollers, drum circles, couples eating convenience store food. Tokyo being itself, for free.
experiences.why_this_matters: This is where Tokyo relaxes. The combination of forest, open grass, and human theater is unscripted and endlessly interesting. Sunday is the day to visit.
experiences.practical_tips: Harajuku or Yoyogi station. Free entry. The rockabilly dancers gather near the Harajuku gate on Sundays. The park connects to Meiji Shrine for a quieter follow-up.

experiences.name: Meiji Shrine morning visit
experiences.description: Through a 12-meter torii gate and down a kilometer of forested path, the Meiji Shrine feels removed from the city around it. At dawn, the sounds disappear. The inner garden has irises in June and golden leaves in November.
experiences.why_this_matters: The Meiji Shrine's forest (70 hectares of 120,000 trees donated from across Japan in 1920) represents the Japanese concept of forest as sacred space. At sunrise, it's as peaceful as any place in Tokyo.
experiences.practical_tips: Free entry. The shrine opens at sunrise. Morning prayer ceremonies happen daily — stand back respectfully. The iris garden (¥500) is worth it in June.

experiences.name: Izakaya evening in Yurakucho under the tracks
experiences.description: Under the Yamanote Line tracks at Yurakucho station, a row of tiny izakayas (Japanese pub-restaurants) has operated since the 1950s. Order yakitori, cold Sapporo, and edamame. Every 5 minutes a train thunders overhead. Japanese salarymen toast loudly beside you.
experiences.why_this_matters: The izakaya culture — loud, unpretentious, communal — is as central to Japanese social life as the tea ceremony. The Yurakucho track-side bars represent this in its most unfiltered form.
experiences.practical_tips: Just walk under the tracks from Yurakucho station toward the Hibiya Park side. Any place with a handwritten menu and no English signage is good. Communicate by pointing. They're used to it.

experiences.name: Sumida River evening boat
experiences.description: The Tokyo Cruise from Asakusa to Hamarikyu (or vice versa) travels along the Sumida River past 12 bridges, the Tokyo Skytree, and the neon edge of the city. At dusk, the river reflects the city lights. This is how Edo (old Tokyo) connected its neighborhoods.
experiences.why_this_matters: Tokyo was a water city before it was a car city. The Sumida River at dusk, seeing the Skytree and the old city simultaneously, provides a perspective the train system cannot.
experiences.practical_tips: Tokyo Cruise runs every 30-40 minutes between Asakusa and Hamarikyu. ¥1,000-1,200. Buy tickets at the pier. The upper deck is best in good weather.

food_scene.name: Ramen (tonkotsu/shoyu/miso)
food_scene.where: Any shop with a line, Shinjuku or Shibuya
food_scene.tourist_trap_warning: Never eat ramen in a place with tourist photos. The best ramen shops are simple, cash-only, with handwritten menus. If there's a line, it's good.

food_scene.name: Onigiri (rice triangles) from 7-Eleven
food_scene.tourist_trap_warning: Japanese convenience store food is genuinely excellent — not a compromise. 7-Eleven and Lawson onigiri are better than most restaurant snacks elsewhere in the world.

food_scene.name: Fresh sushi at Tsukiji outer market
food_scene.tourist_trap_warning: The inner market (Toyosu) now handles the main auctions. The outer market remains excellent for fresh sushi breakfast.

photography_spots.name: Nezu Shrine torii gate tunnel
photography_spots.tip: The vermillion gates tunnel up the hill. Morning light filters through the gaps between gates in April-May.

photography_spots.name: Shibuya Crossing from above
photography_spots.tip: Mag's Park (free) on Shibuya Mark City gives a direct overhead view. Prime time is Friday evening rush hour.

practical_tips.transport: Get a Suica or Pasmo IC card immediately at the airport. It works on all trains, subways, and buses, and at convenience stores. Japan's train system is the best in the world.
practical_tips.etiquette: No talking on the phone on trains. Eat at designated food areas, not while walking. Queue for trains at the marked positions on the platform. Bow when thanking people.
practical_tips.money: Japan is still largely cash-based. 7-Eleven ATMs accept foreign cards. Tipping is not done in Japan — it can confuse or embarrass people.
practical_tips.language: Japanese matters. Google Translate's camera function reads Japanese menus. Learning 'sumimasen' (excuse me) and 'arigatou gozaimasu' (thank you very much) goes far.
practical_tips.best_kept_secret: JR Pass holders can ride the Narita Express, but for the city itself, Suica is far more flexible. The best neighborhoods (Yanaka, Shimokitazawa, Koenji) are all easily accessible on JR.

march.note: Cherry blossom season approaches. Cool and fresh.

april.note: Peak cherry blossom. One of the best months to visit.

may.note: Excellent. Warm, low humidity, golden light.

september.note: Hot and humid. Typhoon season ends. Early autumn color by end of month.

october.note: Best month. Clear skies, autumn color, perfect temperature.

november.note: Autumn foliage at its peak. Crisp, photogenic.
